value.body: A flight dispatcher works in an airline's operations control centre and shares responsibility with the captain for planning each flight safely. They prepare the route, fuel and load plans, check weather and notices to airmen, brief the crew and track flights in progress. The job is shift-based and ground-based, and suits CPL holders who want to stay close to flying.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Class 12 (or a degree) plus DGCA-approved flight dispatcher training; a CPL or its ground subjects help

items.label: Key knowledge
items.value: Air navigation, aviation meteorology, air regulations, aircraft performance

items.label: Aircraft with Indian scheduled airlines
items.note: Aircraft endorsed on airline operator certificates
items.source: MoCA reply in Rajya Sabha (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: CPL holders and CPL ground-subject passers already cover much of the dispatch syllabus. Most still complete a DGCA-approved flight dispatcher course and then airline-specific training and checks before working independently.

value.title: At a glance
items: A ground role; it does not add flying hours.
Next roles: senior dispatcher, operations controller, or crew scheduling and planning roles.
Shift and night work are common; openings depend on airline expansion.

value.title: Domestic air passengers carried
value.note: Calendar years, rounded. 2022 was still recovering from Covid-19. Passenger numbers indicate airline activity, not dispatcher openings.
